text:
chen: seeing a sharp p95 spike for shared-gpu-pool-c this morning, started ~06:12 UTC. dashboard shows p95 48ms -> 420ms, throughput down ~18%. rolling window aligns with a flurry of large batched jobs.
sam: saw the alert from infra-bot too. any pinned tenants? could be a single heavy tenant folding the batcher.
infra-bot: [ALERT] pool=shared-gpu-pool-c metric=p95_latency value=420ms threshold=200ms sts=1976543200
maya: quick note — kernel-switch logs show several kernel_autoswitch events around the same timeframe. attaching a tiny excerpt.
maya: ```
2026-03-18T06:12:14Z kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_v2 reason=seq_len>64 fallback=matmul_v1
2026-03-18T06:12:17Z kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_v1 reason=resource_pressure fallback=matmul_v2
2026-03-18T06:12:18Z kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_v2 reason=batcher_heuristic
```
chen: that flip-flop looks suspicious — switching kernels per-request causes cache/TLB churn and higher tail. also seeing KV cache eviction spikes for tenant ids starting with "acme-".
eli: I ran a perf profile on one of the affected nodes. flamegraph shows heavy stalls in cudaMemcpy followed by stalls in kernel_launch_wait. suspecting contention from big attention kernels.
sam: tenant list: acme-analytics (high QPS, long seqs), beta-search (moderate), internal-eval (sporadic). acme-analytics had a burst at 06:10 with 16 concurrent large requests.
ops: can we throttle acme-analytics temporarily or move it to a dedicated burst pool? we have capacity in reserved-dedicated-2.
devx: proposed quick mitigation: apply per-tenant concurrency cap (concurrency_limit=6) and raise batcher small-request bias so tiny requests don't get grouped with long-context jobs.
chen: before we patch, can someone post the raw KV eviction counters? I want eviction_rate, avg_kv_slots, and prefix_hit_ratio for the window.
maya: eviction snippet: ```
window=06:08-06:20 evictions=12421 avg_slots=312 prefix_hit=0.63
baseline_evictions=120 avg_slots=410 prefix_hit=0.92
``` 
maya: huge jump in evictions; prefix hit plummeted.
eli: hypothesis: long seq jobs cause batcher to increase sequence-length-aware kernel, but when a small request gets batched with a long one, kernel selection flips and KV caches get invalidated due to different KV slot indexing. leads to thrash.
sam: agree. we also have observed that our batcher heuristic uses an aggressive coalescing window when pool util > 70%. that could be combining small and large requests.
chen: quick test idea: change batcher config `coalesce_by_size=false` and `max_batch_seq_gap=16` for pool-c to avoid mixing huge seqs with short ones. patch below.
devx: ```json
{"pool":"shared-gpu-pool-c","coalesce_by_size":false,"max_batch_seq_gap":16,"per_tenant_concurrency":6}
```
ops: I can flip that on for canary nodes in pool-c now. will monitor p95.
infra-bot: [ACTION] applied config to node-17, node-18 canary. monitor-id=cfg-1976543210
sam: also adding a short-term quota: acme-analytics QPS cap=20 for 15m.
chen: after canary toggle p95 dropped to ~70ms on node-17 within 90s. node-18 trending similar. good signal.
maya: KV eviction rate on canary nodes back near baseline: evictions=210 window 06:22-06:30.
eli: still want a follow-up: the kernel selector should avoid per-request flip if the same GPU sees mixed seq distributions within a small interval. we should add hysteresis to kernel selection (min_duration=200ms) to reduce thrash.
devx: filed a follow-up RFC: rfc/kernel-selector-hysteresis PR#442, cc @eng-runtime
chen: great job. ops keep acme throttle for 15m, then we re-evaluate moving them to dedicated if traffic pattern persists. closing slack thread after postmortem notes.
ops: :thumbsup: will hold till 06:50 and then lift if stable.
devx: adding retrospective checklist: sample traces, kernel-switch counts, kv-eviction deltas, batcher-coalesce events. will aggregate into incident doc.
chen: thanks everyone. leaving logs and trace ids in #incidents list.
